bottom_line_fact.text: The S&P 500 Software Index is in a bear market with RSI at 18 (most oversold since 1990) and EV/sales near 8x, down from ~11.5-11.6x, with IGV over 20% below its 200-day moving average.

bottom_line_inference.text: If the AI-disruption fear is overdone, the extreme oversold and valuation readings in software could represent an entry point, but the article does not quantify what growth/terminal-value impairment the price already discounts.

disconfirming_observables: Continued software underperformance despite RSI below 30
Evidence of actual SaaS revenue/seat erosion from agentic AI tools
lower_priority_if: SaaS companies report accelerating revenue erosion from AI tools
EV/sales keeps compressing on worsening fundamentals

near_term_view.text: Software is at extreme oversold and depressed valuation levels now, an immediately investigable dislocation.

hypotheses.next_research_step: Assess whether agentic AI tools (Claude Code) are materially displacing SaaS revenue/seats, and compare current software EV/sales against estimated growth/terminal-value impairment to judge if the sell-off is overdone.

opposing_explanations.text: The valuation collapse could instead signal a structurally lower growth rate and terminal value for software companies due to permanent AI disruption, making the sector a value trap.

hypotheses.premise_condition: if you believe Claude Code is just another DeepSeek moment rather than permanent AI disruption of software
raise_priority_if: Software RSI stays sub-30 while fundamentals (billings, net retention) hold up
Evidence that agentic AI adoption has not dented SaaS revenue

structural_view.text: The long-term AI macro thesis stands and companies leaning into AI will be rewarded, but more volatility is likely.

hypotheses.title: Indiscriminate software sell-off oversold the whole software sector

transmission_chain.text: Agentic AI (Anthropic/Claude Code) could let users replace traditional SaaS functions, raising fears of software obsolescence.
Software index fell into a bear market; RSI 18, EV/sales fell to ~8x, IGV >20% below 200-day MA.

For the bear case to hold, software growth rates and terminal value must be structurally lower; otherwise current earnings power is intact and the selling is indiscriminate (model inference on what would need to be true).

unknowns: Whether Claude Code/agentic AI permanently erodes SaaS revenue or is a transient scare
What degree of growth/terminal-value impairment is already priced into the ~8x EV/sales
Whether oversold RSI readings reliably precede inflows this cycle (article notes few are buying)

bottom_line_fact.text: Stocks that should benefit from AI (hyperscalers, chipmakers, materials) also fell in the software sell-off, and hyperscaler capex forecasts (Meta, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft) were scorned, which the author calls indiscriminate selling.

bottom_line_inference.text: If AI software disruption actually requires physical build-out, the infrastructure names sold off alongside software may be mispriced, but the article does not quantify the capex volumes or earnings impact.

disconfirming_observables: Hyperscaler capex cuts or guidance reductions
Continued infrastructure stock declines on weakening demand signals
lower_priority_if: Evidence AI build requires far less physical infrastructure

near_term_view.text: Infrastructure names have been swept into the sell-off now, but the article frames their benefit as long term.

hypotheses.next_research_step: Check whether hyperscaler capex guidance (Meta, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft) and chip/materials orders remain intact, and gauge how far AI-infrastructure names fell relative to unchanged demand fundamentals.

opposing_explanations.text: If AI disruption is real but doesn't require much new physical investment (a DeepSeek-style efficiency leap), the infrastructure build thesis weakens.

raise_priority_if: Hyperscalers reaffirm or raise capex while their shares stay depressed
Chip/materials demand signals hold despite the sell-off
